🇮🇷🚠 Iran Proposes Overland Internet Corridors to Reduce Reliance on Undersea Cables

Iran has proposed linking national fiber-optic networks across borders to give international internet traffic alternative routes when submarine cables fail. The plan would use overland connections through West Asia to strengthen communications between Asian and European markets.

Deputy communications minister Behzad Akbari presented the “Global Digital Resilience Corridors Initiative” at a resilience session during the International Telecommunication Union conference in Doha. Iran is seeking support from the UN agency and offering its existing network infrastructure to regional and global partners.

The mechanism starts at border crossings, where neighboring countries would connect their fiber networks into international corridors. More direct routes could shorten the distance data travels and reduce delays, while additional paths would give operators more options when a major connection goes down.

Submarine cables would remain essential, but land routes could carry traffic around disruptions affecting them. Coordinating how operators use those alternatives during an outage is part of the proposal, alongside making the corridors commercially viable in normal conditions.

For Iran, the opportunity is to turn its position between regional markets into a larger role in carrying international data. Sharing its fiber network could make the country a transit partner for neighbors seeking more connections to the Persian Gulf and onward markets.

A related initiative is already under discussion with Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan. The three countries have reached a preliminary understanding on a digital corridor linking Central Asia to the Persian Gulf, with the details still subject to negotiation and a final agreement pending.

Delivery will require joint investment and agreements between governments and network operators. The broader proposal also calls for cooperation on data centers, cloud services and cybersecurity; it does not establish that new corridors have been funded, built or activated.

If implemented, these links would give participating countries more control over how their data reaches foreign markets and more options for keeping services running during cable disruptions. Iran’s practical offer is to make its domestic infrastructure part of that regional backup.

Спецы из индустрии бодро отстрелялись про транзакционные данные и площадки с товарами, пока их юная соперница пыталась подглядеть в телефоне и даже почти запомнила уже прозвучавший ответ про финтех-медиа.

🔳🔳🔳🔳🔳: в США оказалось незаконно сносить шпионское ПО со своего телевизора. 

Современные Smart TV используют технологию ACR, которая следит за тем, что вы смотрите, и отправляет данные на серваки. Слежка работает даже при подключении приставки через HDMI.

Какие-либо изменения настроек не особо помогают — так, народ прознал, что один из телевизоров Samsung передавал данные даже после отключения отслеживания в настройках.

Снести же всю эту дрянь мешает закон об авторских правах DMCA — он запрещает обходить программную защиту устройств. Сейчас активисты добиваются разрешения на удаление подобных систем.
